issues.display_title: Issue #643: Mappedin import: group imported levels by building (wizard step 2 + editor Add Floor)
issues.main_description_html:
Group imported Mappedin levels under their building names in the import review experience, in both Create New Project wizard step 2 and the editor Add Floor import. In the editor, imported buildings are preserved by default instead of being forced into the currently selected building.

PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-mappedin-import-building-grouping/prd.md
Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-mappedin-import-building-grouping/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/mappedin-import-building-grouping

Problem

A Mappedin ZIP can contain many levels across more than one building, but the review modal shows them as one long flat list. For malls, hospitals, campuses, and mixed-use venues the user has to work out which levels belong together before committing the import — slow to scan, easy to accept the wrong structure.

In the editor the problem is worse: Add Floor imported every level straight into the currently selected building, mixing levels from different buildings with no review step.

Scope

  1. Wizard step 2 — import review groups levels by building (collapsible sections).
  2. Editor Add Floor — same grouped review modal before anything is added; imported buildings preserved.

Requirements

ID Requirement Priority
R1 Wizard step 2 import review groups imported levels by building. Must
R2 Editor Add Floor import review groups imported levels by building. Must
R3 Each imported building section can be collapsed and expanded. Must
R4 Each building section shows the building name. Must
R5 Each building section shows how many levels it contains. Must
R6 Each building section shows an object count when available. Should
R7 Each expanded building shows its imported levels. Must
R8 Each level row shows the level name. Must
R9 Each level row shows the level height. Must
R10 Each level row shows the level object count. Must
R11 Each level row keeps a thumbnail or placeholder area. Must
R12 The first building is expanded by default. Should
R13 Single-building imports remain quick to review. Must
R14 Wizard import preserves building/level grouping when continuing to the editor. Must
R15 Editor Add Floor import shows the review modal before adding imported levels. Must
R16 Editor Add Floor import preserves imported buildings by default. Must
R17 Editor Add Floor import does not force all imported levels into the selected building. Must
R18 Existing image upload behavior remains unchanged. Must
R19 Existing Add Floor Only and Add & Scan Floor behavior remains unchanged. Must
R20 The UI avoids exposing raw ids, internal names, or technical file structure. Must

Out of scope

  • Editing building or level names inside the review modal.
  • Moving levels between buildings during review.
  • Choosing a different target building during editor import.
  • Changing image upload, Add Floor Only, or Add & Scan Floor behavior.
  • New import formats.

Acceptance checklist

  • Wizard step 2 import review groups levels by imported building.
  • Editor Add Floor import review groups levels by imported building.
  • Each building section can collapse and expand.
  • Each building section shows a readable building name and its level count.
  • Expanded building sections show level rows with name, height, and object count.
  • Level rows keep a thumbnail or placeholder area.
  • The first building is expanded by default.
  • Single-building imports remain simple to review.
  • Wizard Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings and levels.
  • Editor Add Floor import shows review before adding content.
  • Editor import preserves imported buildings by default and does not force levels into the selected building.
  • Existing project content is not overwritten by editor import.
  • Image upload still works in wizard step 2; Add Floor Only and Add & Scan Floor still work in the editor.
  • Copy is clear, plain, and non-technical.

Manual verification

  1. New project → wizard step 2 → import a multi-building Mappedin ZIP.
  2. Confirm the review modal shows collapsible building sections; expand each and check its levels.
  3. Continue to the editor and confirm buildings + levels are preserved.
  4. Open an existing project → Add Floor → import the same ZIP.
  5. Confirm the same grouped review appears and that confirming adds the imported buildings without overwriting existing content.
  6. Import a single-building file and confirm the review stays simple.

Where the building data came from

No new backend work and no mock: a Mappedin ZIP already declares its buildings in floor-stacks.json ({ id, floors[], details.name } — a floor stack is a building). The parser was flattening that grouping away. It is now carried through the pipeline: parseMappedinExport → detectSource → extractFloors (ImportFloor.buildingId) → groupFloorsByBuilding → the modal.

Fallbacks: a zip without floor-stacks.json becomes one building named after the venue; a Mappedin editor .json/.txt export (no stacks concept) falls back to a single "Building 1" section.

Review modal (wizard + editor)

  • BuildingGroupSection.tsx (new) — collapsible building card. Whole header is the toggle (aria-expanded / aria-controls), building glyph, name, and a 4 floors · 1,615 objects summary that stays readable while collapsed. Expanded levels are nested under a spine + connectors; level badges are numbered per building, so every building starts at 1.
  • FloorListSection.tsx — renders building groups instead of a flat list, with a Grouped into N buildings line and an Expand all / Collapse all control (only when there is more than one building). First building expanded by default (R12).
  • Floors with no raster show the geometry glyph used by the Step 2 list rather than a broken-image icon — a Mappedin floor is parsed geometry, not a failed image.
  • groupBuildings.ts (new, pure) — declaration-order grouping, per-building object totals, positional name fallback (Building 1), and a trailing group so a floor with an unknown/absent building is never dropped.

Editor Add Floor

  • useAddLevel.handleImport now parses client-side with the same runImport as the wizard and opens the grouped review modal (variant="editor", copy: "These buildings and floors will be added to your project." → Cancel / Add to Project). Nothing is written until the user confirms (R15). The old /api/import/* calls were dropped from this path.
  • mergeIntoProject.ts (new, pure) — each reviewed building is appended as its own Building record and each level is stamped with its own building, never selectedBuildingId (R16/R17). Levels get fresh ids; existing levels, buildings, and floor configs are untouched.
  • Guard worth knowing: in a project that has levels but no building records, those levels sit in the implicit default building, which levelsInBuilding resolves as buildings[0]. Appending an imported building would have made the import first and silently adopted the user's existing floors — so the merge materializes a real "Untitled building" record and stamps the existing levels with it first. Covered by a test.

Behavior changes to note

  • For a single imported floor, the "Floor name" field in the Add Floor modal no longer overrides the name from the file — the file's name is used, matching what the review modal showed (R8).
  • Mappedin editor .json/.txt imports now go through the client parser instead of /api/import/mappedin-editor. A raw MapThru floorplan .txt still commits directly (it is not a Mappedin import).

Files

New: src/components/setup/import-mappedin/BuildingGroupSection.tsx, src/lib/mappedin-import/groupBuildings.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts
Changed: src/components/setup/import-mappedin/{FloorListSection,ImportSummaryModal,ImportModalActions,types}.tsx|ts, src/components/editor/AddLevelModal.tsx, src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts, src/lib/mappedin/{parse,types}.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/{detectSource,extractFloors,runImport}.ts

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 993 pass (11 new tests across groupBuildings and mergeIntoProject). Two pre-existing failures are unrelated and untouched by this work: mappedin-editor/convert (missing samples/ dir) and api/upload/route (Windows /tmp path).
